nodes.label: Three-lens phase-completion review (dev, user, security)
nodes.rationale: Triggered by Ivan's 'full stack review please, dont ship things before checking' after the build was marked shipped prematurely. Three separate agents plus a controller-run live backtest against Seoul and the local Docker stack -- the separation is what surfaced the contradiction that resolved the fixture collision.

nodes.label: HIGH-1: organiser could self-accredit their own event
nodes.rationale: events_organizer_update_own carried no column restriction, both accrediting_body_id and cpd_hours held a table UPDATE grant, and cpd_hours was bounded only by > 0 -- so every registrant with a verified licence at the targeted body earned a permanent unrevocable credit that body never authorised. Closed at the grant layer (migration 20260725144446), not at RLS. The agent's claim that anon was also exposed was corrected: anon has no UPDATE policy, so its grant was inert.

nodes.label: HIGH-2: attendance_verified minted by possession of an emailed code
nodes.rationale: self_check_in enforced no time window and no checkin_modes.self_serve check, and its predicate was only status <> 'attended' -- while 'cancelled' is a legal registrations.status. Pre-build this forged a correctable flag; post-build it wrote an unrevocable regulator-facing row. Guards added inside the issuance definer.

nodes.label: HIGH-3: false finding that tamper-evidence was broken
nodes.rationale: The agent read the superseded original hash in migration 20260709250000. Live compute_credit_ledger_hash() and verify_ledger_chain() both cover all 18 columns and pin TimeZone/DateStyle/bytea_output; 20260709260000_credit_ledger_hardening had already fixed exactly this. No action taken -- recorded because passing it through unchecked would have falsely told Ivan the product's central claim was broken.

nodes.label: seed.sql blanket grant silently re-opened HIGH-1
nodes.rationale: The migration's own self-verifying DO block passed, then seed.sql -- which runs AFTER migrations -- re-granted events UPDATE and undid the lock. Only running `supabase db reset` afterwards caught it. Without the fix, CI replay-from-zero and the future Singapore provisioning would both have produced an unprotected database. Found by running, not by reading.

nodes.label: Self-inflicted over-revoke of service_role on events
nodes.rationale: The seed.sql fix stripped events UPDATE from service_role too, so seed-demo.ts died with 42501 on the CPD-config write. service_role is the trusted server-side configuration path (seed, dashboard bulk actions, edit fallback) and the migration never revoked it -- only seed.sql diverged. Found by running the seed, not by re-reading grant assertions.

nodes.label: Organiser-to-body authorisation model (deferred product question)
nodes.rationale: Which organisations may legitimately claim a relationship with which accrediting body is a B2 registry decision needing the accrediting-body conversation. Inventing one mid-hardening would have baked in policy nobody agreed to. No live exposure today because only the seed script can set the columns. Re-entry: before ANY surface lets a non-service-role actor set events.accrediting_body_id.

nodes.label: Generous +/-24h credit window
nodes.rationale: Kills the real fraud (never attend, POST the emailed code days later) but is not semantically right -- presence should mean the event's own check-in window. Cannot be tightened yet: the demo fixture registers at Beat 3 and checks in at Beat 4 ~170 min before start, and registration closes exactly when the check-in window opens, so the agent's proposed start-minus-2h bound would have broken the demo outright.

nodes.label: The Karen Lau fixture collision
nodes.rationale: Two distinct auth users shared the display name 'Karen Lau' -- the keynote speaker credited organiser_attested at Beat 5, and the attendee credited attendance_verified at Beat 4.6. The run sheet told the operator to say they 'coexist on the same person', which in front of an accrediting body asserts sanctioned double-counting plus a speaker earning attendance credit at their own session. Practitioner renamed to Dr. Elaine Tsang and decoupled from the keynote.

nodes.label: demo-run-sheet.md (Beat 4.6 CPD readout)
nodes.rationale: Four corrections, all live-verified: Beat 4.6's readout was literally unexecutable (promised a credit_ledger view filtered by name, but that table holds only UUIDs), its trigger cue named the wrong moment (the credit fires on the staff scan, not the later self-serve tap), it did not warn that ledger-demo.ts burns the single-use check-in, and its reset paragraph described behaviour the script does not have.

nodes.label: ledger-demo.ts (bypasses the Server Action)
nodes.rationale: Its step 3 calls self_check_in via a direct RPC that bypasses the Server Action, so the attendee becomes attended with NO credit issued and Beat 4.6 comes back empty with no error anywhere -- a silent failure across the demo's most important beat.

nodes.label: reset-demo.ts
nodes.rationale: Clears credit_ledger outright and reuses the account (contrary to the run sheet's claim of residue accumulation and a fresh auth account each time); now also cleans k.lau@demo.test, which it had been leaving behind.

nodes.label: compute_credit_ledger_hash()
nodes.rationale: Covers all 18 columns and pins TimeZone, DateStyle and bytea_output so the digest is reproducible across session settings.

nodes.label: I1: supabaseAdmin() outside the try (response inversion)
nodes.rationale: It reads process.env with non-null assertions, so a misconfigured deploy throws AFTER mark_attended commits -- the exact response inversion Runtime Contract invariant 1 forbids. Moved inside; the new test was proven red-then-green by restoring the bug and confirming only that test failed.

nodes.label: I2: reconcile-event.ts printed attendee full_name
nodes.rationale: A Hard Rule 10 (no PII in logs) violation found independently by all three review lenses. Now prints registration UUIDs, its target DB, and distinguishes a bad event id from 'nobody attended'.

nodes.label: MEDIUM-1: idempotency index narrower than every comment claimed
nodes.rationale: It was tier-scoped, so a second credit_earned at another tier did not conflict -- leaving no DB backstop for Sprint 3b's organiser-attested issuance. Widened to entry_type='credit_earned' after first verifying zero existing rows violate the tighter rule.

nodes.label: Stage 8 event-config freeze trigger
nodes.rationale: Built on Ivan's 'finish stage 8', applied to Seoul, live-verified and regression-tested. Its needless service_role grant was later removed (LOW-3). The local Docker stack was missing it entirely, so the demo -- which targets local -- would have run without the guard prod had.

nodes.label: Verify findings live; verify your own fixes live
nodes.rationale: Every static gate -- tsc, eslint, 470 vitest tests, next build -- passed green while both authorisation holes were open and the run sheet held a factually false statement meant to be said aloud to a regulator. The review itself needed reviewing: one HIGH was false, two agents contradicted each other on a matter of fact, and the fix for the deepest finding introduced its own regression that surfaced only by executing the demo seed.

nodes.label: The premature 'all stages shipped' claim
nodes.rationale: The claim went into PROJECT_STATE.md and the vault note before any review had run. Corrected -- and the correction was recorded rather than quietly rewritten, which is why the failure is inspectable at all.

hyperedges.label: Authorisation holes and regressions found by lenses + live runs, not gates
